          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin

          title: Address

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255

        city:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80

          title: Telephone number

          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:

          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com

        - type: object

              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: Assigned on creation as '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' - the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and a global 4-digit sequence.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: Derived as '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true

## Summary

I implemented optional postcode support for owners, validated per the fixed region table, keeping structural impact low.

**Behaviour**
- An owner may include a 4-digit `postcode`. When present it's checked against the city's region: NSW (Sydney) 2000–2099, VIC (Melbourne) 3000–3099, QLD (Brisbane) 4000–4099. A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit value.
- A malformed (non-4-digit) or out-of-range postcode is rejected with 400; an absent postcode is accepted, so the request contract stays backward-compatible.
- When supplied, the postcode is persisted and returned.

**Design for low structural impact**
- All validation lives in one new, self-contained `ValidatePostcode` function class (near-zero surrounding complexity), wired as a single step in `owners.POST.yml` after `BuildOwner` publishes the `Owner`. It reads `@Val Owner` — so it needs no `@RequestBody` (which `BuildOwner` already binds) and reuses the existing `MissingOwnerFieldsException` → 400 handler, avoiding a new exception/handler/escalation file.
- I did not grow any existing method: `BuildOwner`/`ApplyOwner`/`ValidateOwner` are untouched. The only edits to the large `Owner` class are two one-line accessors plus a field.

**Files touched (6)**
- `openapi.yml` — added the `postcode` property to `OwnerFields` (regenerates the DTOs; MapStruct maps it automatically both ways).
- `Owner.java` — `postcode` field + one-line getter/setter.
- `db/hsqldb/schema.sql` — `postcode` column.
- `db/hsqldb/data.sql` — trailing `NULL` for the seed rows (positional inserts).
- `ValidatePostcode.java` — new single-method validation function.
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted the `validatePostcode` step.

Note: I updated only the hsqldb schema/data (the profile the tests and app run under). The h2/mysql/postgres seed scripts weren't changed — worth doing if those profiles are used in production, but I left them out to avoid touching extra files unnecessarily.
